title: STUDY TOPIC Loving righteousness Part 2
devotional:
Righteousness is expressed in whole hearted commitment,

In Matthew 5:48 Jesus said: -

“Be perfect therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.’’

Many read these words and think Jesus is asking us to live sinless lives. However, the word Perfect (teleios) does not mean sinless perfection, but wholeheartedness and stands for total commitment. Righteous living will encourage whole hearted commitment to Jesus.

Righteous living means that we won’t have to perform in order to gain acceptance or approval. One of the things that Jesus does in the Sermon of the Mount, is that He contrasts authentic God pleasing righteousness with the phony, external righteousness of His day. The Pharisees craved for the acceptance and approval of others, and this became their motivation for doing ‘spiritual’ things like ‘giving to the poor, praying and fasting.’ They practice spiritual disciplines without having a heart for God. They were hypocrites. It is important we understand what the bible means when it talks about hypocrites.

‘‘A hypocrite is not a person who falls short of their high ideas or occasionally sins, because all Christians experience these failures. A hypocrite deliberately uses religion to cover up their sins and promote their own gains.” Warren W. Wiersbe. Source unknown

So to be a hypocrite is much more serious than living an inconsistent life, it is the deliberate use of religious activity to deceive others and hide your own sin and failure in order to promote a false image about yourself, in order to get the approval of others.

Righteousness will produce in us a sense of security and well being.

Righteousness results in a person feeling secure and loved, it enhances us as people. It is so easy because of our feelings of insecurity to pervert our religious activity into religious showmanship. It is our insecurities that cause us to live for the approval of others.

“Ultimately our only reason for pleasing men around us is that we may please ourselves. Our real desire is not to please others as such; we want to please them because we know that, if we do, they will think better of us. In other words, we are pleasing ourselves and are merely concerned about self-gratification.” Lloyd Jones.

kingschurchlkld.com. Accessed 31/07/25

Doing spiritual “things” is not a guarantee or proof that we are spiritual people. Our desire for acceptance, approval and recognition from others can turn our spiritual activities and Christian service into expressions of selfishness and self-centredness devoid of any authentic righteousness. What we are in private, where no one sees us, is who we really are.

So many Christians are too tired to live righteous lives. I have met so many Christians who are completely exhausted, for years they have been trying to keep up a façade, trying to win the approval and acceptance of others, trying to fit in, trying to earn God’s love and blessing. This way of living has robbed them of passion and enthusiasm, their spark has gone, their colour has faded, and all they have is a reputation, a reputation for being ‘committed,’ a reputation that is not really worth having.

Righteous living is really just an appropriate response to the love of God our Father. Twelve times in Matthew 6, Jesus mentions the word Father. This is quite amazing. Jesus did not give us a list of rules, or ‘dos’ or ‘don't s,’ rather he talks a lot about God as father. Look a Matthew 6:1, 4,6(x2), 8, 9, 14, 15, 18(x2), 26, and 32.

Authentic righteousness is the result of being in a relationship with God as your father

For too long we have lived with the idea that to be holy or righteous is a drab and boring life. This is a distortion of the truth. Those who receive and enjoy God’s love and experience Him as Father will know the joy and freedom of living a life of righteousness.
prayer: Father may the joy of righteousness fill my life.
